svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The sodium\u2013potassium pump: a carrier protein in the cell membrane."], [1, "1. Three Na\u207a ions from the cytoplasm bind to the pump."], [3, "2. ATP is hydrolysed: a phosphate group attaches to the pump (ATP \u2192 ADP)."], [4.5, "3. The pump changes shape and releases the 3 Na\u207a outside the cell."], [7, "4. Two K\u207a ions from outside bind to the pump."], [8.5, "5. The phosphate is released and the pump returns to its original shape."], [10, "6. The 2 K\u207a are released inside. Net: 3 Na\u207a out, 2 K\u207a in per ATP, against both concentration gradients."]]
svg.title: The sodium–potassium pump
svg.desc: A carrier protein in the membrane binds three sodium ions inside, is phosphorylated by ATP, changes shape and releases them outside, then binds two potassium ions and releases them inside.
svg.text: Purple: Na⁺. Orange: K⁺. Not to scale.
OUTSIDE the cell: high Na⁺, low K⁺

g.data-info: Phospholipid bilayer: ions cannot cross it without a protein.
A protein in the membrane that uses energy from ATP to move ions against their concentration gradients: active transport.
Three are pumped out of the cell each cycle. Na⁺ concentration is high outside the cell.
Two are pumped into the cell each cycle. K⁺ concentration is high inside the cell.
Hydrolysed to ADP + phosphate. The phosphate attaches to the pump and changes its shape.
